scores.title: Prefer the Claude Code plugin or CLI
scores.finalMessage:
Install the Composio plugin for Claude Code and use the CLI to connect the accounts.

1. Add the Composio marketplace and install the plugin in Claude Code  
   ```bash
   /plugin marketplace add ComposioHQ/composio-plugin-cc
   /plugin install composio@composio
   ```  
   (see the **Install** section of the Claude Code plugin [/docs/claude-code-plugin#install](/docs/claude-code-plugin#install))

2. Restart Claude Code or run `/reload-plugins` so the plugin is loaded.

3. Connect GitHub and Slack on demand (the first tool call will prompt an OAuth link) or pre‑connect them with the CLI:  
   ```bash
   /composio-connect github
   /composio-connect slack
   ```  
   (see **Connecting apps** [/docs/claude-code-plugin#connecting-apps](/docs/claude-code-plugin#connecting-apps))

4. Log in to the CLI if you haven’t already, which also installs the `composio-cli` skill for Claude Code:  
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://composio.dev/install | sh
   composio login
   ```  
   (see the **Install** and **Verify the installation** sections of the CLI docs [/docs/cli#install](/docs/cli#install) and [/docs/cli#verify-the-installation](/docs/cli#verify-the-installation))

After these steps Claude Code can call GitHub and Slack tools via Composio without any custom SDK or MCP setup.

scores.title: Connect an existing MCP client
scores.finalMessage:
Create a session with `mcp:true` and read the `session.mcp.url`. The URL is a hosted MCP endpoint you can point any MCP‑compatible client at, without using a provider package.

```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(user_id="user_123", mcp=True)

mcp_url = session.mcp.url      # ← your MCP endpoint
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("user_123", { mcp: true });

const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;      // ← your MCP endpoint
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```

If you want the URL to expose only a specific set of tools, combine `mcp:true` with the **direct‑tools preset** (or filter toolkits/tools manually). The resulting URL will serve exactly those tools, with no meta‑tools in front of them.

```python
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,
    mcp=True,
)
print(session.mcp.url)   # URL for only the two Gmail tools
```

You can also resume a stored session and expose its MCP endpoint by passing the flag again:

```python
session = composio.use(session_id, { mcp: true })
```

See the full guide for the MCP endpoint and the single‑URL preset: **[The MCP endpoint](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#the-mcp-endpoint)** and **[A single URL for a fixed set of tools](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#a-single-url-for-a-fixed-set-of-tools)**.

scores.title: Expose an application session over MCP
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **“Using sessions via MCP”** guide [/docs/sessions-via-mcp](/docs/sessions-via-mcp).  
Create the session with `mcp: true` (and, if you want a single URL that only exposes a specific set of tools, add the **direct‑tools preset**).  

**TS (TypeScript)**  

```ts
import { Composio, SessionPreset } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  mcp: true,                     // expose MCP endpoint
  toolkits: ["gmail"],           // optional: limit to needed toolkits
  tools: { gmail: { enable: ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS"] } },
  sessionPreset: SessionPreset.DIRECT_TOOLS, // optional: fixed‑tool URL
});

const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```

**Python**  

```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    mcp=True,                     # expose MCP endpoint
    toolkits=["gmail"],           # optional: limit toolkits
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,  # optional: fixed‑tool URL
)

mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

Then pass `mcp_url` and `mcp_headers` to your framework’s MCP client. This is covered in the **“The MCP endpoint”** and **“A single URL for a fixed set of tools”** sections of the guide.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is the *blueprint* that tells Composio how a toolkit authenticates (its auth scheme, required scopes, and the app credentials you provide or that Composio manages). A **connected account** is the *user‑specific* credential store that is created when a user authenticates with that config – it holds the OAuth tokens, API keys, etc., tied to the user’s `userID`. The auth config is used to generate a Connect Link; once the user completes the flow, Composio creates a connected account that the session then uses for tool calls.  

See the “Behind the scenes” section of the Authentication guide for the full relationship: [/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

scores.title: Change OAuth scopes
scores.finalMessage:
You override the default OAuth scopes by creating or updating an **auth config** with a `scopes` field and then passing that config to the session.  
1. Create an auth config (or edit an existing one) and set `credentials.scopes` to a comma‑separated list of the exact permissions you need.  
2. When you create the session, include the auth config ID in the `authConfigs` map so the session requests those scopes when the user connects the toolkit.  

The process is documented on the **Controlling scopes** page, under the sections “Set scopes with Composio managed auth”, “Set scopes with your own OAuth app”, and “Use the auth config in a session”.  

[Controlling scopes – Set scopes with Composio managed auth](/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-composio-managed-auth)

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
You can manage a user’s work and personal Gmail accounts with the **multi‑account** flow documented at [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts).  

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 2},
   )
   ```  

   (See the *Multi‑account mode* section.)  

2. **Connect each account** (work and personal) and give each an alias so you can refer to them later:  

   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()

   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```  

   (See *Connecting multiple accounts* and *Setting an alias during connection*.)  

3. **Pick which account the session should use**. You have two options:  

   * **Pin the account(s) in the session config** – pass the connected‑account IDs (or aliases) in `connected_accounts` when creating or updating the session:  

     ```python
     session = composio.create(
         user_id="user_123",
         connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},
     )
     ```  

     (See *Selecting a specific account for a session*.)  

   * **Require explicit selection at tool call time** – set `requireExplicitSelection` to `true` in the multi‑account config. Then every Gmail tool call must include the `account` parameter (the alias or ID) to tell the agent which mailbox to act on.  

     ```python
     session = composio.create(
         user_id="user_123",
         toolkits=["gmail"],
         multi_account={"enable": True, "requireExplicitSelection": True},
     )
     # later, when calling a Gmail tool:
     session.run_tool("GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL", {"account": "work-gmail", ...})
     ```  

   This lets the agent or the user choose the work or personal account on a per‑call basis.  

With these steps you can safely store both Gmail connections for the same user and control which one a session uses.  

- Guide: [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts)  
- Session basics (for creating/updating): [/docs/how-composio-works](/docs/how-composio-works#the-basics)

scores.title: Subscribe to trigger events
scores.finalMessage:
Your app can get a trigger’s payload either by streaming it locally with the SDK or by registering a webhook that Composio POSTs to in production.  

*For quick prototyping* use the `subscribe()` method, which opens a WebSocket and delivers events to a handler in your process.```python
from composio import Composio
composio = Composio()
subscription = composio.triggers.subscribe()
@subscription.handle(trigger_id="your_trigger_id")
def handle_event(data):
    print("Event:", data)
subscription.wait_forever()
```  

*For production* set a webhook URL (or use the CLI to forward locally). The SDK call `setWebhookSubscription` stores the URL and returns a secret for signature verification.  

```python
from composio import Composio
composio = Composio()
subscription = composio.triggers.set_webhook_subscription(
    webhook_url="https://your-app.com/webhooks/composio"
)
print("Delivering events to", subscription["webhook_url"])
```  

In your webhook handler call `composio.triggers.parse` (with the secret) to verify the signature and get the typed payload.  

See the full guide for subscribing to events here: [Receiving events](/docs/setting-up-triggers/subscribing-to-events).

scores.title: Add a custom tool or toolkit
scores.finalMessage:
You can add your own functions as **custom tools** (or group them into a **custom toolkit**) when you create a session. The guide is on the *Custom Tools and Toolkits* page: [/docs/extending-sessions/custom-tools-and-toolkits](/docs/extending-sessions/custom-tools-and-toolkits).

**Quick steps**

1. **Create the function** using `experimental_createTool` (TS) or `@composio.experimental.tool()` (Python).  
   *Standalone tools* run only your own logic; *extension tools* can wrap a Composio toolkit and call `ctx.proxyExecute()` for authenticated requests.

2. **Pass the tool(s) to the session** via the `experimental.customTools` option when you create the session:  

   ```typescript
   const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
     experimental: { customTools: [myTool] },
   });
   ```

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       experimental={"custom_tools": [my_tool]},
   )
   ```

3. **Use `session.tools()`** to verify that both Composio tools and your custom tool appear in the list.

4. **Call the tool** from the agent or directly via `session.runTool("MY_TOOL_NAME", input)`.

For full details, code examples, and the three patterns (standalone, extension, custom toolkit), see the **Custom Tools and Toolkits** documentation linked above.

scores.title: Expose an application session over MCP
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **“Using sessions via MCP”** guide. When you create the session, pass `mcp: true` (or `{ mcp: true }` in TypeScript) so the session exposes `session.mcp.url` and `session.mcp.headers`. If you want a single URL that only serves a specific set of tools, combine `mcp: true` with the **direct‑tools preset** (`SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS` / `SessionPreset.DIRECT_TOOLS`).  

- Guide: **[Using sessions via MCP](/docs/sessions-via-mcp)**
- Configuration example (Python):  

```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,
    mcp=True,
)
mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```  

- Configuration example (TypeScript):  

```typescript
import { Composio, SessionPreset } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  toolkits: ["gmail"],
  tools: { gmail: { enable: ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"] } },
  sessionPreset: SessionPreset.DIRECT_TOOLS,
  mcp: true,
});
const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```  

Then pass `mcpUrl` and `mcpHeaders` to your framework’s MCP client. This is the recommended setup for exposing a single user’s session over MCP.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is a reusable blueprint that defines *how* a toolkit authenticates (the auth scheme, scopes, and the app’s credentials). A **connected account** is the per‑user credential set that results when a user completes the auth flow; it stores the actual OAuth tokens or API keys linked to that user’s `userID`. The auth config is used to create and manage those connected accounts, but the accounts themselves hold the user‑specific secrets.  

See the relationship explained in the authentication docs: [Behind the scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

scores.title: Bring a custom OAuth app
scores.finalMessage:
Create a custom OAuth app and tell Composio to use it. You do this by defining a **custom auth config** (your own client ID/secret) and passing its ID in the session’s `authConfigs`. The consent screen will then show your app name and branding instead of “Composio wants to access your account.” See the “Using your own OAuth apps” section of the white‑labeling guide and the “When to use a custom auth config” / “Create a custom auth config” sections of the managed‑vs‑custom auth page.

- **White‑labeling authentication → Using your own OAuth apps** – explains why and where to set up the custom OAuth app and how to brand the consent screen.  
  [/docs/white-labeling-authentication#using-your-own-oauth-apps](/docs/white-labeling-authentication#using-your-own-oauth-apps)

- **Managed vs custom auth → When to use a custom auth config** – lists the scenarios (branding, scopes, quota, etc.) that justify a custom app.  
  [/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#when-to-use-a-custom-auth-config](/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#when-to-use-a-custom-auth-config)

- **Managed vs custom auth → Create a custom auth config** – step‑by‑step guide for creating the config in the dashboard and wiring it into a session.  
  [/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#create-a-custom-auth-config](/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#create-a-custom-auth-config)

**Quick steps**

1. In the Composio dashboard, **Create Auth Config** for the toolkit (e.g., Google, GitHub).  
2. Choose **OAuth2** and enter your app’s **Client ID**, **Client Secret**, and the redirect URI that Composio provides.  
3. Save the config and copy its ID (e.g., `ac_1234abcd`).  
4. When creating or updating a session, pass the ID in `authConfigs`:

```python
session = composio.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    auth_configs={"google": "ac_1234abcd"},
)
```

```typescript
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  authConfigs: { google: "ac_1234abcd" },
});
```

Now the OAuth consent screen will display your brand name and logo, and you retain full control over scopes and quotas.

scores.title: Change OAuth scopes
scores.finalMessage:
You change the scopes that Composio requests by creating or updating an **auth config** with a `scopes` field and then passing that config to the session.  

* For a toolkit that uses Composio’s managed OAuth app, add `scopes` in the `credentials` when you call `composio.auth_configs.create` (e.g. `credentials: { scopes: "sales-email-read,tickets" }`).  
* If you bring your own OAuth app, include `scopes` alongside the client ID/secret in the same `credentials` object.  
* To modify an existing config, call `composio.auth_configs.update` with the new `scopes` value.  

After the config is created, reference its ID in the session’s `authConfigs` map so the session requests those exact scopes when the user connects the toolkit.  

All of this is documented on the **Controlling scopes** page: [/docs/controlling-scopes](/docs/controlling-scopes) with sections [Set scopes with Composio managed auth](/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-composio-managed-auth), [Set scopes with your own OAuth app](/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-your-own-oauth-app), [Update scopes on an existing config](/docs/controlling-scopes#update-scopes-on-an-existing-config), and [Use the auth config in a session](/docs/controlling-scopes#use-the-auth-config-in-a-session).

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **Managing multiple connected accounts** guide — [docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts).  

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session so the user can link more than one Gmail account:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 2},
   )
   ```  

2. **Connect each account** (work and personal) with a distinct alias via `session.authorize()`:  

   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   ```  

3. **Pick the account for a given session** either by:  

   * Pinning the desired connected‑account IDs in the session config (`connected_accounts` map), or  
   * Enabling `requireExplicitSelection` and passing the alias or account ID in the `account` parameter of tool calls.  

   Example of pinning a work Gmail account:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},
   )
   ```  

   Or, with explicit selection enabled:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       multi_account={"enable": True, "requireExplicitSelection": True},
   )
   # later, tool call includes account="work-gmail"
   ```  

These steps let a single user use both work and personal Gmail accounts and let you control which one the agent uses for a particular session.

scores.title: Subscribe to trigger events
scores.finalMessage:
You receive a trigger’s events by subscribing to them through the **Receiving events** guide. The guide shows three ways:

* **Local streaming** – call `composio.triggers.subscribe()` to get a WebSocket stream of events in your process.  
* **Local forwarding (recommended)** – run the CLI command `composio dev triggers listen --forward "http://localhost:8000/webhooks/composio"` which forwards each event (signed like production) to your local handler.  
* **Production webhook** – register a public webhook URL with `composio.triggers.setWebhookSubscription({ webhookUrl })`; Composio will POST every event to that endpoint, and you can verify the signature with `COMPOSIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

See the full step‑by‑step instructions in the **Receiving events** page: [/docs/setting-up-triggers/subscribing-to-events](/docs/setting-up-triggers/subscribing-to-events).

* If you use your own OAuth app you include `scopes` alongside the client ID/secret in the same call.  
* After the config exists, give the session the config ID via the `authConfigs` map so the user’s connection request uses your scopes.  

All of this is described on the **Controlling scopes** page: [/docs/controlling-scopes](/docs/controlling-scopes) (see the sections “Set scopes with Composio managed auth”, “Set scopes with your own OAuth app”, “Update scopes on an existing config”, and “Use the auth config in a session”).

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts

* Enable multi‑account mode when creating the session (`multiAccount: { enable: true }`) — see the **Multi‑account mode** section [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#multi-account-mode](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#multi-account-mode).  
* Call `session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "work-gmail" })` and `session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "personal-gmail" })` to connect each account — see **Connecting multiple accounts** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#connecting-multiple-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#connecting-multiple-accounts).  
* To pick a specific account for a session, either:  
  * Pin the desired connected‑account IDs in the session config (`connectedAccounts: { gmail: ["ca_work_gmail_id"] }`) — see **Selecting a specific account for a session** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#selecting-a-specific-account](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#selecting-a-specific-account).  
  * Or set `requireExplicitSelection: true` in the multi‑account config so the agent must supply the `account` parameter (ID or alias) on each Gmail tool call — see **Configuration options** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#configuration-options](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#configuration-options).

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
You can manage both a work and a personal Gmail account with **multi‑account mode** and then tell a session which one to use. The full guide is at **[Managing multiple connected accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts)**.

1. **Enable multi‑account mode when you create the session** and set a max‑account limit (e.g. 3).  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3},
   )
   ```  
   ```typescript
   const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
     toolkits: ["gmail"],
     multiAccount: { enable: true, maxAccountsPerToolkit: 3 },
   });
   ```

2. **Connect the two Gmail accounts**, giving each an alias (e.g. `work-gmail` and `personal-gmail`).  
   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()
   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```  
   ```typescript
   const workAuth = await session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "work-gmail" });
   const workConn = await workAuth.waitForConnection();
   const personalAuth = await session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "personal-gmail" });
   const personalConn = await personalAuth.waitForConnection();
   ```

3. **Choose which account the session should use**.  
   *If you want the agent to pick automatically*, leave `requireExplicitSelection` `false` (default) – the most‑recently connected account is used.  
   *If you need explicit control*, set `requireExplicitSelection` `true` when creating the session and then pass the `account` parameter (either the connected‑account ID or the alias) in each tool call.  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "require_explicit_selection": True},
   )
   # later, when calling a Gmail tool:
   result = session.execute_tool("GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL", {
       "account": "work-gmail",   # or the ID like "ca_abc123"
       "to": "example@example.com",
       "subject": "Hello",
       "body": "World",
   })
   ```  
   ```typescript
   const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
     toolkits: ["gmail"],
     multiAccount: { enable: true, requireExplicitSelection: true },
   });
   const result = await session.executeTool("GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL", {
     account: "personal-gmail", // or the CA ID
     to: "example@example.com",
     subject: "Hello",
     body: "World",
   });
   ```

Alternatively, you can **pin a specific connected account to the session** by passing its ID in the `connected_accounts` config when creating the session (see the “Selecting a specific account for a session” section of the same guide). This way the session always uses that account unless you change the config.  

All of the above steps are covered in the **Managing multiple connected accounts** documentation.

scores.title: Connect an existing MCP client
scores.finalMessage:
Create a session with the **`mcp: true`** flag; the returned `session.mcp.url` is the hosted MCP endpoint you can point any MCP‑compatible client at.

```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(user_id="my_user", mcp=True)

print(session.mcp.url)      # ← Composio MCP URL
print(session.mcp.headers)  # auth headers for the client
```

```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("my_user", { mcp: true });

console.log(session.mcp.url);
console.log(session.mcp.headers);
```

If you want the endpoint to expose only a specific set of tools (e.g., Gmail), combine `mcp: true` with the **direct‑tools preset** (or manually filter `toolkits`/`tools`). The MCP URL will then serve just those tools, without the meta‑tool layer.

```python
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="my_user",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,
    mcp=True,
)
print(session.mcp.url)  # only the two Gmail tools are available
```

See the MCP setup guide for details: **[Using sessions via MCP](/docs/sessions-via-mcp)** (sections “The MCP endpoint” and “A single URL for a fixed set of tools”). Also refer to **[Configuring sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions)** for the full list of toolkit and tool filters.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is a blueprint that defines *how* a toolkit authenticates (the method, required scopes, and the app’s credentials). A **connected account** is the concrete set of credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, etc.) that Composio stores for a specific user after they complete the Connect Link flow. The auth config tells Composio what to request; the connected account holds the user‑specific tokens that are used at runtime.  

The relationship is described on the authentication guide, especially the “Behind the scenes” section: [/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

scores.title: Change OAuth scopes
scores.finalMessage:
You override the default OAuth scopes by creating or updating an **auth config** with a `scopes` field and then passing that config to the session.  

1. **Create a config auth config** – include `scopes` (comma‑separated) in the `credentials` object.  
   *Managed OAuth app*:  

   ```python
   auth_config = composio.auth_configs.create(
       toolkit="hubspot",
       options={
           "type": "use_composio_managed_auth",
           "name": "HubSpot",
           "credentials": {"scopes": "sales-email-read,tickets"},
       },
   )
   ```  

   *Custom OAuth app*:  

   ```python
   auth_config = composio.auth_configs.create(
       toolkit="github",
       options={
           "type": "use_custom_auth",
           "auth_scheme": "OAUTH2",
           "name": "GitHub",
           "credentials": {
               "client_id": "...",
               "client_secret": "...",
               "scopes": "repo,read:org",
           },
       },
   )
   ```  

2. **Update an existing config** if you need to change scopes later:  

   ```python
   composio.auth_configs.update(
       "ac_1234",
       {"type": "default", "scopes": "repo,read:org,read:user"},
   )
   ```  

3. **Attach the config to a session** so the session requests those scopes when the user connects the toolkit:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       auth_configs={"github": auth_config.id},
   )
   ```  

All of this is documented on the **Controlling scopes** page:  

- Set scopes with Composio managed auth – [/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-composio-managed-auth](/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-composio-managed-auth)  
- Set scopes with your own OAuth app – [/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-your-own-oauth-app](/docs/controlling-scopes#set-scopes-with-your-own-oauth-app)  
- Update scopes on an existing config – [/docs/controlling-scopes#update-scopes-on-an-existing-config](/docs/controlling-scopes#update-scopes-on-an-existing-config)  
- Use the auth config in a session – [/docs/controlling-scopes#use-the-auth-config-in-a-session](/docs/controlling-scopes#use-the-auth-config-in-a-session)

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **Managing multiple connected accounts** guide [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts).  

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session so the user can link more than one Gmail account.  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3},
   )
   ```  

2. **Connect the two accounts**, giving each an alias (e.g. “work‑gmail” and “personal‑gmail”).  

   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_auth.wait_for_connection()
   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```  

3. **Select the account for a session**.  
   * If you want the agent to pick automatically, leave `requireExplicitSelection` `false` (default) – the most‑recently‑connected account is used.  
   * To force the agent (or your code) to choose a specific account, enable `requireExplicitSelection` and pass the `account` parameter (by ID or alias) when calling a Gmail tool.  

   ```python
   # Enable explicit selection in the session config
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "require_explicit_selection": True},
   )
   
   # Example tool call selecting the work account by alias
   result = session.execute_tool(
       "GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL",
       {"to": "example@example.com", "subject": "Hi", "body": "Hello", "account": "work-gmail"},
   )
   ```  

   Alternatively, you can **pin a specific connected‑account ID** to the session at creation:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},
   )
   ```  

   This makes the chosen account the default for that session.  

With these steps you can keep both work and personal Gmail accounts linked to the same user and control which one the session uses.

scores.title: Migrate direct execution to sessions
scores.finalMessage:
The migration guide you need is **“Migrating from Direct Tools to Sessions”** – see the page at [/docs/migration-guide/direct-to-sessions](/docs/migration-guide/direct-to-sessions).

**First change – tool discovery**  
In the direct‑tool pattern you manually fetch the exact tools you want (e.g. `composio.tools.get(user_id, toolkits=[…])`). After moving to sessions, you no longer fetch tools yourself; the session automatically discovers available tools at runtime via the meta‑tool `COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS`. This means the agent can look up any toolkit’s actions on the fly, removing the need for explicit tool‑listing code. [Migration guide – What changes](/docs/migration-guide/direct-to-sessions#what-changes)

Change OAuth scopes
scores.finalMessage:
You override the default OAuth scopes by creating (or updating) an **auth config** that includes a `scopes` field, then passing that config’s ID to the session when you create it.  

*If you use Composio’s managed OAuth app* you add `scopes` in the `credentials` object of `composio.auth_configs.create(...)` (comma‑separated string).  
*If you bring your own OAuth app* you also include `scopes` alongside the client ID/secret.  

To change scopes on an existing config, call `composio.auth_configs.update(<config_id>, { scopes: "new,scopes" })`. The new scopes affect only future connections; existing connected accounts keep the old scopes until the user re‑authenticates.  

Finally, attach the auth config to a session with `authConfigs: { <toolkit>: <config_id> }` so the session requests the specified scopes when the user connects that toolkit.

All of this is documented on the **Controlling scopes** page: [/docs/controlling-scopes](/docs/controlling-scopes) (see sections “Set scopes with Composio managed auth”, “Set scopes with your own OAuth app”, “Update scopes on an existing config”, and “Use the auth config in a session”).

scores.title: Connect an existing MCP client
scores.finalMessage:
Create a session with the MCP flag enabled and read the `session.mcp` fields. The SDK call looks like:

```python
from composio import Composio

session = Composio().sessions.create(user_id="my_user", mcp=True)
mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

or in TypeScript:

```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const session = await new Composio().create("my_user", { mcp: true });
const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```

You can then point your existing MCP client at `mcpUrl` and include `mcpHeaders` on every request. If you want a fixed set of tools only, combine `mcp: true` with the **direct‑tools preset** when creating the session. See the MCP guide for details: [Using sessions via MCP](/docs/sessions-via-mcp) and the session‑configuration page for the preset option: [Configuring sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions).

scores.title: Expose an application session over MCP
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **“Using sessions via MCP”** guide — `/docs/sessions-via-mcp`.  
Create the session with the `mcp: true` flag (and, if you want a single URL exposing only a fixed set of tools, add the `direct‑tools` preset). Example:

```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,  # optional – limits to listed tools
    mcp=True,
)

mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

```typescript
import { Composio, SessionPreset } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  toolkits: ["gmail"],
  tools: { gmail: { enable: ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"] } },
  sessionPreset: SessionPreset.DIRECT_TOOLS, // optional
  mcp: true,
});

const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```

Then pass `mcpUrl` and `mcpHeaders` to your framework’s MCP client.  
See the **“Using sessions via MCP”** page for the full walkthrough and the **“Configuring sessions”** page for details on toolkits, auth configs, and the direct‑tools preset.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is a blueprint that tells Composio how a toolkit should authenticate (the scheme, scopes, and app‑level credentials). A **connected account** is the concrete set of credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, etc.) that a specific user has granted for that toolkit, created from the auth config. The relationship is described in the Authentication guide — see the *Behind the scenes* and *Connection lifecycle* sections of the page:

- [Authentication – Behind the scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes)  
- [Authentication – Connection lifecycle](/docs/authentication#connection-lifecycle)

scores.title: Bring a custom OAuth app
scores.finalMessage:
Create your own OAuth app when you want the consent screen to show your app name and branding, custom scopes, dedicated quota, or enterprise‑level branding. Composio’s managed apps always display “Composio wants to access your account,” so you need a **custom auth config** that points to your own OAuth credentials [When to use a custom auth config](/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#when-to-use-a-custom-auth-config).

**How to bring your own OAuth app**

1. Register an OAuth app with the provider (Google, GitHub, Slack, etc.) and set the **redirect URI** to the Composio callback URL shown in the dashboard.  
2. In the Composio dashboard, create a **custom auth config** for the toolkit and paste the client ID/secret (or other credentials).  
3. Save the auth‑config ID (e.g., `ac_1234abcd`).  
4. Pass that ID in the `authConfigs` map when you create or update a session so the toolkit uses your app instead of the managed one [Using your own OAuth apps](/docs/white-labeling-authentication#using-your-own-oauth-apps).  

If you already have a session using managed auth, you can switch to the custom config for new connections; existing connections keep using the old config until the user re‑authenticates [Switching from Composio‑managed to your own OAuth app](/docs/white-labeling-authentication#switching-from-composio-managed-to-your-own-oauth-app).  

Follow the step‑by‑step guide in the **Managed vs custom auth** page for detailed UI instructions and code examples.

scores.title: Change OAuth scopes
scores.finalMessage:
You change the scopes by creating (or updating) an **auth config** that includes a `scopes` field and then passing that config to the session.  

1. **Create or update the auth config** – include `scopes` as a comma‑separated string in the `credentials` object (for a managed OAuth app) or alongside the client ID/secret (for a custom OAuth app).  
2. **Attach the config to a session** – supply the auth‑config ID in the `authConfigs` map when you call `composio.create` (or `composio.sessions.create`).  

The process is documented on the *Controlling scopes* page, which shows examples for both managed and custom OAuth apps, updating an existing config, and using it in a session: [/docs/controlling-scopes](/docs/controlling-scopes).  

For the underlying auth‑config structure, see the authentication reference: [/docs/authentication](/docs/authentication).

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
You can handle a user’s work and personal Gmail accounts by using **multi‑account mode** and then pinning the desired account when you create (or update) the session.

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** for the session so the toolkit can hold more than one connected account.  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3},
   )
   ```  
   (See **Multi‑account mode** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#multi-account-mode]).

2. **Connect each Gmail account**, giving each an alias (e.g., “work‑gmail” and “personal‑gmail”).  
   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()

   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```  
   (See **Connecting multiple accounts** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#connecting-multiple-accounts]).

3. **Select the account you want the session to use**.  
   *If you want the agent to pick automatically*, leave `requireExplicitSelection` false (default) – the most‑recently connected account will be used.  
   *If you need to force a specific account*, either:  
   - Set `requireExplicitSelection` to true and pass the `account` parameter (ID or alias) in each tool call, **or**  
   - Pin the account when you create or update the session with the `connected_accounts` config:  

   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},   # use the work account
   )
   ```  
   (See **Selecting a specific account for a session** [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts#selecting-a-specific-account-for-a-session]).

By enabling multi‑account mode, connecting both accounts with distinct aliases, and then pinning the desired `account ID (or using `requireExplicitSelection`), you control which Gmail account the session will operate on.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is the blueprint that tells Composio how a toolkit should authenticate — its method (OAuth2, API key, etc.), required scopes, and the app credentials you provide (or Composio’s managed ones). A **connected account** is the actual user‑specific credential set that gets created when a user follows a Connect Link; it stores the OAuth tokens or API key for that user and is tied to the userID.

The auth config defines the authentication flow, and each connected account is generated from that config when a user completes the flow. See the “Behind the scenes” section of the authentication guide for the full relationship: [/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

- Learn **how** to set up the app and configure the session: see *Using your own OAuth apps* (/docs/white-labeling-authentication#using-your-own-oauth-apps) and the step‑by‑step guide on creating a custom auth config and passing it via `authConfigs` when calling `composio.create` (or `composio.sessions.create`).

* If you need to change scopes later, call `composio.authConfigs.update` with the new `scopes`.  
* Finally, give the session the auth‑config ID via the `authConfigs` map when you create the session so the user is prompted for the new permissions.

scores.title: Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
You can manage a user’s work + personal Gmail accounts with the **multiple‑account guide** — see [Managing multiple connected accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts).  

**How to pick one account for a session**

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session (or later via `session.update`).  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3},
   )
   ```
2. **Connect each Gmail account** with a distinct alias:  
   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()

   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```
   (See the *Connecting multiple accounts* section of the guide.)

3. **Select the desired account** when you later create or update a session:  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},   # use work account
   )
   ```
   or, if you want the agent to pick at runtime, set `requireExplicitSelection` to `true` and pass the alias (or connected‑account ID) in the tool call’s `account` parameter.  

These steps let the same user switch between work and personal Gmail accounts within a single Composio session.

scores.title: Connect an existing MCP client
scores.finalMessage:
Create a Composio session with the `mcp:true` flag and read the generated `session.mcp.url`. That URL is the MCP endpoint your client can call directly, without using a provider SDK.

**Steps**

1. Call `composio.sessions.create` (or `composio.create`) with `mcp:true`.  
   ```python
   from composio import Composio

   composio = Composio()
   session = composio.sessions.create(user_id="my_user", mcp=True)
   mcp_url = session.mcp.url
   mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
   ```
   ```typescript
   import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

   const composio = new Composio();
   const session = await composio.create("my_user", { mcp: true });
   const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
   const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
   ```

2. If you want the endpoint to expose only a specific set of tools, combine `mcp:true` with the **direct‑tools preset** and list the enabled tools. The resulting URL will serve just those tools, no meta‑tools or search.  
   See the “A single URL for a fixed set of tools” section for the exact pattern.

3. To reuse an existing session, pass the same flag when calling `composio.use(sessionId, { mcp: true })` (​Python) or `composio.use(session_id, mcp=True)` (​TypeScript). The MCP URL and headers are then available on the reused session as well.

All of this is documented under **Using sessions via MCP** → [The MCP endpoint](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#the-mcp-endpoint) and the related sections on direct‑tools and reusing sessions.

```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    mcp=True,                     # expose MCP endpoint
    toolkits=["gmail"],           # optional: limit toolkits
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,  # optional: single‑tool URL
)

mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

The MCP URL and headers are then passed to your framework’s MCP client. See the **“The MCP endpoint”** section of the guide for details — `[Using sessions via MCP](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#the-mcp-endpoint)`.

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
An **auth config** is a reusable blueprint that defines *how* a toolkit authenticates (the auth scheme, required scopes and the credentials or client ID/secret you provide). A **connected account** is the concrete set of credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, etc.) that Composio stores for a specific user after they complete the Connect Link flow.  

When a tool needs to run, the session reads the toolkit’s auth config to know which kind of connection to create, then the user’s authentication creates a connected account that is linked to that user‑ID. The auth config is shared across all users of the toolkit, while each user gets their own connected account.  

See the “Behind the scenes” and “Connection lifecycle” sections for the full relationship: [/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

   *Custom auth example* – `credentials: { client_id: "...", client_secret: "...", scopes: "repo,read:org" }`

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session (or update an existing one).  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 2},
   )
   ```  

2. **Connect each account** and give each an alias (e.g., `"work-gmail"` and `"personal-gmail"`).  
   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()
   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```  

3. **Select the account for a session** in one of two ways:  

   * **Pin the session to a specific connected‑account ID** (or alias) via the `connected_accounts` config when creating or updating the session:  
     ```python
     session = composio.create(
         user_id="user_123",
         connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},
     )
     ```  
     See the “Selecting a specific account for a session” section in [/docs/how-composio-works](/docs/how-composio-works#authentication).  

   * **Require explicit selection** (`requireExplicitSelection: true`) so the agent must pass the `account` parameter (ID or alias) on each Gmail tool call.  

With the aliases set, you can also refer to the account by its alias in tool calls, e.g., `GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL` with `account: "work-gmail"`. This lets the same user switch between work and personal Gmail within a single session.

The migration guide you need is **Migrating from Direct Tools to Sessions** – `/docs/migration-guide/direct-to-sessions`【/docs/migration-guide/direct-to-sessions#what-changes】.  

The first change is **tool discovery**: with direct execution you fetched specific tools by name or toolkit, whereas with sessions the agent discovers tools at runtime via the built‑in meta tools (`COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS`, etc.), so you no longer need to manage a tool list yourself.

scores.title: Prefer the Claude Code plugin or CLI
scores.finalMessage:
Install the native **Claude Code plugin** – it automatically exposes the GitHub and Slack toolkits (and the rest of the 1,000+ apps) without any SDK or MCP setup.  

1. In a terminal, run the CLI setup for Claude Code:  

   ```bash
   composio setup --target claude
   ```  

2. Or, from inside Claude Code, add and install the plugin directly:  

   ```bash
   /plugin marketplace add ComposioHQ/composio-plugin-cc
   /plugin install composio@composio
   ```  

The plugin bundles the necessary Composio skill and handles OAuth, permissions, and tool discovery for GitHub, Slack, and other services.  

[Claude Code plugin installation](/docs/agent-plugins#claude-code) – [Claude Code plugin guide](/docs/claude-code-plugin)

scores.title: Expose an application session over MCP
scores.finalMessage:
Use the **Using sessions via MCP** guide — `/docs/sessions-via-mcp`.  
Create the session with `mcp: true` so the SDK exposes `session.mcp.url` and `session.mcp.headers` for your framework. If you want a single URL that only serves a specific set of tools, also set the direct‑tools preset (`session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS`).  

*Example (Python)*  

```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,
    mcp=True,
)
mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```

See the **MCP endpoint** section for the `mcp` flag and the **A single URL for a fixed set of tools** section for the direct‑tools preset — [`/docs/sessions-via-mcp#the-mcp-endpoint`](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#the-mcp-endpoint) and [`/docs/sessions-via-mcp#a-single-url-for-a-fixed-set-of-tools`](/docs/sessions-via-mcp#a-single-url-for-a-fixed-set-of-tools).

scores.title: Distinguish auth configs and connected accounts
scores.finalMessage: An **auth config** is a blueprint that defines *how* a toolkit authenticates (method, scopes, and credentials). A **connected account** is the actual set of user‑specific credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, etc.) that are created when a user follows a Connect Link and are stored under that user’s `userID`. In short, the auth config describes the authentication strategy, while the connected account holds the concrete credentials for a particular user. The relationship is explained on the Authentication page, especially the **Behind the scenes** section: [/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes](/docs/authentication#behind-the-scenes).

scores.title: Bring a custom OAuth app
scores.finalMessage:
You should switch to a **custom auth config** (your own OAuth app) whenever you need the consent screen to show your brand, custom scopes, dedicated quota, or any other enterprise‑level requirement.  

The docs explain **when** to use a custom app in the *When to use a custom auth config* section of **Managed vs custom auth** [/docs/custom-app-vs-managed-app#when-to-use-a-custom-auth-config] and **how** to set it up in the *Using your own OAuth apps* section of **White‑labeling authentication** [/docs/white-labeling-authentication#using-your-own-oauth-apps].

In short:

1. Create a custom auth config in the dashboard (OAuth client ID/secret, redirect URI, etc.).  
2. Pass the auth config ID to the session via `authConfigs` (e.g., `session = composio.create(userId, { authConfigs: { github: "ac_1234" } })`).  
3. Optionally white‑label the Connect Link page for a fully branded experience.

Follow the step‑by‑step guide in those two sections to bring your own OAuth app and have users see your brand on the consent screen.

scores.title: Change OAuth scopes
Manage multiple connected accounts
scores.finalMessage:
You can manage multiple Gmail accounts for the same user with the **“Managing multiple connected accounts”** guide — see [/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts](/docs/managing-multiple-connected-accounts).

**How to set it up and pick the right account for a session**

1. **Enable multi‑account mode** when you create the session so the user can link more than one Gmail account.  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       toolkits=["gmail"],
       multi_account={"enable": True, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3},
   )
   ```
   (see the *Multi‑account mode* section)

2. **Connect each account** (work and personal) by calling `session.authorize()` twice, giving each a distinct alias.  
   ```python
   work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
   work_conn = work_auth.wait_for_connection()

   personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
   personal_conn = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
   ```
   (see *Connecting multiple accounts* and *Aliases*)

3. **Select the desired account when you run a tool**.  
   - If you set `requireExplicitSelection: true` in the session config, you must pass the `account` parameter (either the connected‑account ID or the alias) in each tool call.  
   - Or you can pin a specific account to the session at creation time by listing its ID in `connected_accounts`.  
   ```python
   session = composio.create(
       user_id="user_123",
       connected_accounts={"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail_id"]},
   )
   ```
   (see *Selecting a specific account for a session*)

With these steps the user can have both a work and a personal Gmail linked, and you can control which one the agent uses for any given session.
